blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: replace nouns with direct and indirect object pronouns (lo, la, le, les, me, te, nos, os)
put the pronouns in the right place with conjugated verbs, infinitives, gerunds, the perfect and commands
combine two pronouns correctly (se lo doy, dímelo)
use the pronouns after prepositions (para mí, conmigo)

blocks.text: A direct object answers what / whom? (Compro el pan: what do I buy? the bread). An indirect object answers to / for whom? (Doy el pan a Ana: to whom? to Ana). Pronouns replace them so you do not have to repeat the noun.

items: Only the third person differs between direct and indirect: lo, la, los, las (direct) and le, les (indirect).
Lo replaces a masculine noun (el libro) or a general idea; la a feminine noun (la casa); los / las the plurals.
Le and les are the same for masculine and feminine.

blocks.title: le for a man in Spain
blocks.text: In Spain you will often hear le instead of lo for a man: Le veo instead of Lo veo. This is accepted in Spain (leísmo), but this course uses lo / la.

blocks.title: No "it" as a subject
blocks.text: Dutch het often has no Spanish equivalent: Het regent = Llueve. As an object, het becomes lo / la: Ik zie het = Lo veo.

head: Noun version
Pronoun version
English
rows: Do you see me? Yes, I see you.

blocks.text: The indirect object pronoun is used with dar, decir, escribir, enviar, mandar, regalar, prestar, enseñar, ofrecer, preguntar, explicar, comprar (for someone) and other verbs of giving, telling and showing. In Spanish it is normal to use the pronoun even when the person is named: Le doy el libro a Ana.

head: Spanish
Pronoun version
English
rows: Will you tell me the time? Yes.
Explico la regla a los alumnos.
I explain the rule to the pupils.

head: Verbs like gustar
Example
English
rows: It seems a good idea to me.

head: Situation
Position
Example
rows: before the first verb or attached to the infinitive
Lo voy a comprar. / Voy a comprarlo.
before estar or attached to the gerund (accent)
before haber (never between he and participle)
No lo compres. No me lo digas.

blocks.title: Written accents
blocks.text: When you attach a pronoun, the stress must stay where it was. If that would put it on the third-last syllable or earlier, add an accent: comprar gives comprarlo (no accent), but leyendo gives leyéndolo, compra gives cómpralo and di + me + lo gives dímelo.
Put the indirect before the direct: me lo, te la, nos las. When le or les would come before lo, la, los, las, it becomes se: Le doy el libro gives Se lo doy.

head: Spanish
Replaces
English
rows: I tell it to her / him.
I am going to give it to them.

blocks.title: Order differs from Dutch
blocks.text: Dutch puts the thing first: Ik geef het hem. Spanish puts the person first: Se lo doy (to him / it). Remember: indirect before direct.

head: Person
After a preposition
Example
rows: Voy sin ti. Quiero ir contigo.

items: para mí, a ti, de él, con nosotros, sin ellos: Esto es para mí. Voy sin ti. Hablo de ellos.
conmigo and contigo are single words: ¿Vienes conmigo? Quiero ir contigo.
After entre, según and excepto use yo / tú: entre tú y yo, según tú.
A mí, a ti ... add emphasis: A mí me gusta el té, pero a ti te gusta el café.

rows: The pronoun goes before a conjugated verb.
Voy a comprarlo. / Lo voy a comprar.
Attach to the infinitive or put before the first verb, not between.
le / les become se before lo, la, los, las.
The person you buy it for is an indirect object: le.
Add an accent when attaching a pronoun to a gerund.
Two pronouns on a command need an accent.
After a preposition, use mí, ti, él ...

blocks.text: Replace the noun with a pronoun, or complete the sentence. Answers are on the last page.

items.full: ¿Conoces a mis padres? Sí, los conozco.

items.q: Doy un regalo a Marta. = ______ doy un regalo.
items.full: Doy un regalo a Marta. = Le doy un regalo.

items.q: Escribo una carta a mis padres. = ______ escribo una carta.
items.full: Escribo una carta a mis padres. = Les escribo una carta.
¿Me das el libro? Sí, te lo doy.

items.q: Doy el libro a Pablo. = ______ doy.
items.full: Doy el libro a Pablo. = Se lo doy.

items.q: Voy a comprar el coche. = Voy a ______.
items.full: Voy a comprar el coche. = Voy a comprarlo.
Estoy leyendo el libro. = Estoy leyéndolo.

items.q: ¿Has visto la película? Sí, ______ he visto.
items.full: ¿Has visto la película? Sí, la he visto.
Trae el café. = Tráelo, por favor.

items.q: Do you give it to me?
I am going to tell it to her.
